chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding

a man who bought a slave girl and copulated with her, so she gave birth to a child for him, and her child died. He (peace be upon him) said: If they wish, they sell her to cover the debt that is upon her master from her price, and if she has a child, she is evaluated based on her child from his share.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling a slave girl after her child dies in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the status of an Umm al-Walad (mother of a child) upon the death of her offspring, establishing that the master retains the right to sell her to recover the purchase price debt. It further specifies that if she bears another child, her valuation is adjusted to account for the new child's share, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that each child confers a distinct portion of emancipation value. This ruling underscores the economic and legal interdependence between the slave woman's reproductive status and her master's financial rights in pre-modern Islamic society.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding

a man who bought a slave girl (and) copulated with her. So she gave birth for him to a child, and her child died. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he so desires to, he sells her regarding the debts which happen to be upon her master, from her price, and if there was a child for her, it would be evaluated upon her child from his share’.
